epithet: The great news they could not stop arguing about
lede: Makkah was talking about one thing: the claim that the dead would rise. This surah opens on that buzz of questions, answers it with the world they were standing in, and then sets the Day itself before them, hour by hour.

names.name: al-Nabaʾ
names.note: After the “tremendous news” of its second ayah: the Resurrection — or the Qurʾan that announced it, as others of the early commentators said.

names.name: ʿAmma
names.note: Its first word, in full ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn. Al-Qurṭubī heads it with this name, and it is why the thirtieth juzʾ of the muṣḥaf, which begins here, is everywhere called Juzʾ ʿAmma. Ibn al-Jawzī also records Sūrat al-Tasāʾul, the Questioning.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records the agreement of the commentators that all of it is Makkan, and al-Qurṭubī gives it as Makkan without mention of any other view. The traditional order places it eightieth, among the last surahs revealed before the Hijrah.
revelation.when: The later years in Makkah, when the Resurrection had become the centre of the dispute

evidence.quote: وَيُقالُ لَها: سُورَةُ التَّساؤُلِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ﴿عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: Of everything the Prophet ﷺ taught in Makkah, the point his people found hardest was not the oneness of Allah — they half admitted that — but the return to life. Bones that had crumbled, raised and questioned: they asked one another about it in their gatherings, some denying it outright, some unsure, some mocking.

Ibn al-Jawzī gives the occasion from the commentators in a sentence: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, the idolaters began questioning one another — what is this that he has brought? — and arguing and disputing over it, and the surah came down.{reported}

It does not join the argument. It says twice, “No — they will come to know,” and then asks them to look around: the earth laid out like a bed, the mountains driven in like tent-pegs, sleep, night and day, the lamp of the sun, the rain. Whoever arranged all of that for a purpose did not make its inhabitants for none. Then comes the appointment itself — the Day of Decision — and what waits on either side of it.

occasions.title: What they were asking one another
occasions.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, the idolaters took to questioning one another — “What is it that he has brought?” — and arguing and quarrelling over what he had been sent with. So this was revealed.
occasions.source: Ibn al-Jawzī, from the commentators. Al-Ṭabarī, al-Suyūṭī and al-Shawkānī relate it too.

evidence.quote: قالَ المُفَسِّرُونَ: لَمّا بُعِثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ جَعَلَ المُشْرِكُونَ يَتَساءَلُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ، فَيَقُولُونَ: ما الَّذِي أتى بِهِ؟ ويَتَجادَلُونَ، ويَخْتَصِمُونَ فِيما بُعِثَ بِهِ، فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ

aim: To establish the Resurrection and the Recompense by proofs and evidence.

outline.title: The question
outline.summary: About what are they asking one another? About the tremendous news, over which they disagree. No — they will come to know. Again, no — they will come to know.

outline.title: The evidence
outline.summary: Have We not made the earth a resting place and the mountains its pegs; created you in pairs; made your sleep for rest, the night a covering, the day for livelihood; built seven strong heavens above you and set in them a blazing lamp; and sent down from the rain-clouds water in torrents, to bring out grain and plants and gardens thick with growth?

outline.title: The appointment
outline.summary: The Day of Decision is a time already fixed: the Day the Trumpet is blown and you come in crowds, the sky is opened and becomes gates, and the mountains are set moving until they are a mirage.

outline.title: For the transgressors
outline.summary: Hell lies in wait, a home for those who overstepped, to stay in it for ages. No coolness there and no drink but scalding water and pus: a fitting recompense. They never expected a reckoning, and denied Our signs — and everything We have recorded in a book. “So taste: We shall increase you in nothing but punishment.”

outline.title: For the mindful
outline.summary: A place of success: gardens and vines, companions, a cup that is full. No idle talk there, and no lying. A reward from your Lord, a gift that is enough.

outline.title: The Day the Spirit and the angels stand
outline.summary: Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Most Merciful — none will have the power to address Him. The Spirit and the angels stand in rows, silent but for whom He permits. That Day is the truth; so let whoever wills take a way back to his Lord. The surah closes with the disbeliever’s wish: “If only I were dust.”

keyAyah.why: The hinge of the surah. Everything before it is the argument; everything after it is the Day the argument was about.

virtues.text: Abū Bakr said: “Messenger of Allah, you have gone grey.” He ﷺ said: “Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ‘ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn’ and ‘Idhā l-shamsu kuwwirat’ have turned me grey.”
virtues.arabic: شَيَّبَتْنِي هُودٌ وَالْوَاقِعَةُ وَالْمُرْسَلاَتُ وَعَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ

before: Al-Mursalāt ends by asking the deniers: “In what message after this will they believe?” (77:50). Al-Nabaʾ opens on those same people, still asking one another about it.
after: Al-Nāziʿāt takes up the Day again from its first instant — the souls drawn out, the first blast and the second — and adds the story of one who denied it: Pharaoh.

notable.label: The Day of Decision is an appointed time
The Spirit and the angels stand in rows
